# Session 15: Presentations

## 📋 Agenda

- **8 min + 4 min Q&A** per group
- Course wrap-up

## Format

- **Five slides**, one per report section
- **Every member speaks** to at least one slide
- Confusion matrix **on screen**
- `show_errors` table open and ready

::: {.callout-note}
Your time is for the presentation, not for setting up. Have the notebook open before you start.
:::

## The two questions every group gets

::: {.callout-important}
## 1
**"Show us an item the model got wrong, and say whether the cause was the model or your scheme."**
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## 2
**"What did your QC pass change?"**
:::

Both questions ask about the analysis, not the code. They distinguish *having run the cells* from *having done the work*.

## And a reminder

::: {.callout-tip}
## Your F1 is not graded
A study reporting **0.31** with a clear account of why scores higher than one reporting **0.82** without an account.

A low κ is not a penalty either. It is a finding about your scheme.
:::

# Wrap-up

## What was the same in every track

Whatever you annotated, the pipeline did not change:

```
load gold → format prompt → call model → evaluate → inspect errors
```

. . .

Only the **task** and the **prompt** changed. The pipeline is what transfers to your future work, not any particular model, which will be replaced within a year.

## The one idea

> **An LLM produces annotations, and you must check them against a gold standard before you report them.**

. . .

Checking means: a gold standard you built and can defend · a metric you understand because you once computed it by hand · a frozen run someone else can reproduce · and an accurate account of what your numbers do not show.

. . .

None of this is specific to LLMs. It is what makes any measurement worth reporting.

## Where this goes next

- **Bigger gold sets** — and inter-annotator agreement as a research question in its own right
- **Other constructs** — anything you can define, you can try to annotate
- **The open questions** — contamination, prompt sensitivity, whether "agreement with humans" is the right target at all

. . .

You now have a working pipeline and the practices needed to use it honestly. That is enough to begin your own work.

# Thank you

Deliverables and rubric: the **Final Project** pages.
